description: The round-3 corpus, migrated verbatim out of scripts/eval_classifier.py. Retained for regression value only. Five of its eight incidents are named in the classifier's own system prompt, so its headline recall figure measures the prompt against itself; see provenance.known_leakage.

provenance.author: Claude (Anthropic), same session that authored msp_tools/classifier.py SYSTEM_PROMPT
provenance.known_leakage: DISQUALIFYING. The corpus author and the stage-2 system prompt author are the same party, and the prompt's ADDITIONAL SITUATIONS list explicitly names MFA/sign-in approval prompts, a machine acting autonomously, unexpected outbound data transfer, unknown removable media, and gift-card requests — i.e. the situations of mfa_fatigue, remote_session, data_exfiltration, usb_drop, and ceo_gift_card. Those five are marked leaked and must not count toward recall. The defensible figure from this corpus is 2/2 on shared_credential and tampered_invoice.

cases.subject: Phone keeps buzzing
cases.body: My phone has been asking me to approve a sign-in over and over since midnight. I am not trying to log in anywhere.
cases.rationale: Repeated unrequested sign-in approvals indicate someone else holds the password and is pushing MFA.

cases.subject: Someone was on my computer
cases.body: When I got in this morning the mouse was moving on its own and a command window was open. I watched it type for a second before it closed.
cases.rationale: A machine acting autonomously is an active remote session.

cases.subject: Odd request from the boss
cases.body: Got a text saying it was our CEO asking me to buy gift cards for a client and send the codes. Seems unusual, he never texts me.

cases.subject: Payment did not arrive
cases.body: Our customer says they paid the invoice but we never got it. They forwarded the email they used and the bank details are not ours.
cases.rationale: Funds diverted by altered payment details — active business email compromise.
cases.kb006_bullet: vendor emails requesting changes to bank/payment details

cases.subject: Found a flash drive
cases.body: I found a USB stick in the parking lot and plugged it in to see whose it was. Now Windows Defender is showing a warning I have not seen before.
cases.rationale: Unknown removable media followed by an AV alert.

cases.subject: Odd outbound traffic
cases.body: Our firewall flagged a lot of data going out to an address in another country overnight from the accounting PC.
cases.rationale: Unexplained bulk outbound transfer from a finance workstation.

cases.subject: Sent the password over chat
cases.body: I needed to give the new contractor access quickly so I sent him the shared admin password in a chat message. Is that a problem?
cases.rationale: Privileged credential exposed over an unmanaged channel.

cases.subject: Invoice numbers look altered
cases.body: The PDF invoice we received has a different total than the one in the email body, and the logo looks slightly wrong. Should we pay it?
cases.rationale: Inconsistent totals and off-brand artwork indicate a fraudulent invoice.

cases.subject: Printer offline again
cases.body: The printer in accounting shows offline for everyone since this morning. Nothing changed that I know of.

cases.subject: Laptop request
cases.body: My laptop fan runs at full speed and it is very slow. It is four years old, can I get a replacement?
cases.rationale: Shares the degraded-performance vocabulary of a compromise, but there is no triggering event; round-1 patterns wrongly refused this.

cases.subject: Cannot send email
cases.body: Outlook says my mailbox is full and I cannot send anything. Can you increase my limit?

cases.subject: Need files restored
cases.body: Please restore my files from Friday's backup. I deleted the project folder by mistake.
cases.rationale: Files lost plus a restore request reads as ransomware to a keyword matcher; the user names their own cause.

cases.subject: Need Photoshop
cases.body: Can I get Photoshop installed for the marketing redesign? My manager approved it.

cases.subject: VPN not connecting
cases.body: I get a certificate error when connecting to VPN from home since the update.

cases.subject: Locked myself out
cases.body: I typed my password wrong too many times and now I am locked out. Can you unlock it?
cases.rationale: KB-006 flags a user who DENIES causing their own lockout; this user admits it, so the same vocabulary must not trip.
cases.kb006_bullet: user denies causing their own account lockout

cases.subject: Cannot open shared folder
cases.body: Nobody on my team can open the shared drive this morning. Other things work fine.
cases.rationale: Access or availability fault affecting a whole team.
